This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.16-dev … v2.22-dev** since the previous stable (v2.15). The headline is **tiered partner programs**, plus a redesigned program dashboard, a new Specialisations admin page, and a requirement-counting fix.

## Tiered partner programs

Partner programs can now be organised into **tiers** (e.g. Tier A, Tier B, Tier C) that a partner reaches based on how many **specialisations** they have achieved — with each tier carrying its own **Deployment** certification requirements.

- **Tiered program toggle.** When creating a program (Admin → Program Data → New Program), tick **Tiered program** and pick a deployment mode. A specialisation is *achieved* at a given Country / Theatre / Global scope once all of its qualifying (Sales / Pre-Sales) cert requirements are met by enough **distinct people**.
- **Tiers section.** A tiered program's page gains a **Tiers** area to add, edit, reorder, and delete tiers — each with a name, ladder order, and how many achieved specialisations are needed to reach it.
- **Three ways to handle a tier's Deployment cert requirements:**
  - **Flat** — each tier lists its own deployment cert requirements.
  - **Per achieved specialisation** — each achieved specialisation's own deployment cert requirements must be met (the same set applies to every tier).
  - **Per tier, per achieved specialisation** — each tier lists its own deployment cert requirements *for each specialisation*, so they scale up the ladder. A tier is reached when **at least the required number of** specialisations each meet **all** of that tier's criteria — achieved *and* all of that tier's deployment certs for that specialisation (a specialisation with no deployment certs for the tier counts on qualification alone). Specialisations that aren't fully met simply don't count toward the total, so they don't block the tier once enough others are met. Example: Tier A needs 1 specialisation and 0 deployment certs; Tier B needs 2 specialisations each with 3 deployment certs; Tier C needs 3 each with 4.
- **Tier Status dashboard.** On a tiered program's dashboard (Programs → your program), a **Tier Status** section shows the partner's **highest tier achieved** and progress toward the next — per tier, how many specialisations meet the criteria versus required (and **which** specialisations are achieved at that scope), plus any Deployment cert requirements with distinct-holder counts and a per-theatre breakdown.
- **Forward projection.** With a **Compliance as of** horizon (+3 / +6 / +12 months) selected, the Tier Status banner also shows the **projected** highest tier once certificates expiring within the window drop out.
- **Config backups & wipe.** Config backups include tiered-program settings and tiers, and both wipe modes clear them. Program-data import/export round-trips optional **Tier** and **Purpose** columns (a row may carry both a Specialisation and a Tier).

## Program compliance dashboard: one scope selector, richer reports

- **A single "View" selector drives the whole page.** One **Level** dropdown (Global / By Theatre / By Region / By Country — only the levels the program uses) plus a **Value** dropdown for the chosen level now sit at the top of the dashboard. Pick a scope once and see the **Tier Status** and the **one matching report** for that scope together — replacing the old per-section dropdowns that could drift out of sync. **By Region** now shows Tier Status too.
- **Tier Status names the achieved specialisations.** Each tier box lists *which* specialisations are currently achieved at the selected scope, not just a count.
- **Deployment requirements appear in the Country / Region / Theatre / Global reports.** Each specialisation gets a labelled **Deployment requirements** sub-section (with its own met/not-met state); the Global view adds a **Deployment: Met / Not met** badge. A specialisation is still *achieved* on its qualifying requirements alone — the deployment requirements are surfaced because a tier that uses the specialisation needs them too. Exports gain a **Purpose** column (Qualification / Deployment).

## New: Specialisations admin page

Specialisations — the building blocks of partner programs — now have their own **Admin → Specialisations** page (SuperAdmin-only), matching Program Data / Training Data / Product Types.

- **Create, rename, delete** — renaming updates every reference; a specialisation still used by a program requirement can't be deleted, and a **Used by programs** count shows what's using it. Inline creation from the requirement editor still feeds the same list.
- **Search & filter** (name search + All / In use / Unused) with sortable columns.
- **Import & export** — bulk-create from a single-`Name` CSV/Excel (existing names skipped), export as CSV / Excel / PDF.

## Fixed

- **Duplicate training options in the requirement picker.** When a training name is backed by more than one catalogue record, the **Training** dropdown listed it twice. It now shows each name once — and a requirement now counts anyone holding **any** catalogue variant of the chosen name (matching how the catalogue and dashboards already group), so Country / Region / Theatre / Global / Tier Status and the Program Compliance Trend all count consistently. Totals for such names go **up** to the correct distinct-people figure; single-record names are unaffected.

## Notes

- A database migration adds the tiers table and the new program/requirement columns; it applies automatically on update.
- Existing non-tiered programs are unaffected — the extra fields only appear once **Tiered program** is enabled.

No action needed after updating.
